description: A grid of tiny cells that runs through preset patterns and finally settles into a check or a cross, with a label and an elapsed-time counter.
interactionNotes: The component takes no input and is driven by `status`. In "working" the cells light up one by one with pattern-induced delay and the counter ticks in tenths of a second; moving to "done" or "error" stops the grid, fades the runner layer and the end mark (check or cross) settles in with a slight scale-up while the label swaps with a fade and blur removal.

props.label: Label for the working state.
props.doneLabel: The label that comes before the finish time.
props.errorLabel: The label that comes before the failure time.
props.pattern: Name of a preset pattern, or a custom pattern with a `cells` array.
props.grid: Grid size; any value other than 4 is rounded to 3.
props.color: Color of the cells in the working state.
props.cellSize: Side of each cell, in pixels.
props.fontSize: Text size in pixels; the gap between grid and label is derived from it too.
props.step: Duration of one unit, in milliseconds; the whole cycle = `loop × step × scale`.
props.idleOpacity: Brightness of the cells that are off.
props.glow: Glow halo behind the lit cells.
props.glowColor: Halo color; empty means the same color as the cell.
props.showTimer: Whether the elapsed-time counter is shown.
props.elapsed: Elapsed time in seconds; if provided, the internal counter is turned off.
props.style: Inline style; it rides on the component's variables.

tips: `doneLabel` and `errorLabel` come **before** the time and the counter sits behind them, so it reads "done in 1.4 seconds"; if you know the number of steps, pass `elapsed` so the time comes from your own source instead of the component's stopwatch.

You get ten preset patterns and each only makes sense on some grids: `arrow`/`dots`/`ripple`/`spiral` only on 3×3 and `sweep`/`spin`/`rain`/`pulse` only on 4×4. `orbit` and `snake` have both. If a pattern is not available for the requested grid, it falls back to that grid's default automatically.

For a custom pattern, pass an object instead of a name: `pattern={{ cells: [...], loop: 5, scale: 1.2 }}`. An array shorter than the grid is padded with holes automatically and a longer one is trimmed; `null` means a cell that never lights up.
For a light, low-contrast grid turn on `glow` and give `glowColor` your brand color — since the cells are tiny, the halo is the only thing you notice at first glance.
The whole motion is in CSS, not in JavaScript; only the counter advances on a 100 ms timer. So dozens of loaders on one page carry no noticeable cost.
The end time is announced from `performance.now()` rather than from ticking a count; if the browser sleeps the tab, the counter does not lag behind.
